steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Loosen up that trigger finger, Fiammetta.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: I get the impression that scowl's stuck on your face until you get to fire off a few grenades.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Thinking about that disgusting dream just makes me even angrier.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Too bad it wasn't entirely a dream.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Look over there, waaaaay in the distance.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: The Shrine of Nurtury's still there...

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Let's go, Mostima, to the hospital.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Doesn't matter if what just happened was a dream or not, we need to make sure that—
The fact that I'm the first person you thought of really means something to me, Fiammetta.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Lemuen?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I'm so glad you're alright.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: How're your legs?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: A little sore.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: What happened?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I was running all over that dream until I was dead tired. Getting to sit down is a treat... Alright, alright, the two of you can relax now.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: What the hell's going on here?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: (Shakes head) It was only my second day after being created cardinal, and I was headed to the office like usual. It might have been the moment I stepped out the front door, or maybe when I saw the Shrine...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I can't really say when I left reality. It all happened so naturally.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: What is it, Fiammetta?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Salvete, everyone.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Cap—

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Y-You're still keeping—

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: What are you up to, wearing that?!

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: A friend kept it for me. You have a very kind junior, Fiammetta.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: She told me this wasn't something to just throw away. Perhaps today, I will finally reach my destination. To be clothed in these vestments as I do so may be fate at work.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Why you...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Andoain has an important role to play. Resolving your existing disputes is not a priority—

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: It's been a while, Federico.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I know who you are and how you like to get things done, and I know that according to the Curia's rules, saints have the highest authority in emergency situations... But please give us a little time.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Please keep it brief.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: The last time the four of us got together like this was that fateful mission, wasn't it?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: It's been ten years.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: We reached the underground palace, Fiammetta got a distress signal from another team and went to go help them, while Andoain was revising our tactics at the entrance.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: We laughed as we shared the last of the chestnut scones... An old habit of our team. I remember the day well.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: We were so happy back then... I thought those days would never end. Nobody could've imagined what would come next.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: You caused all this, Andoain, but you still refuse to tell the truth, or at least repent.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Our brief time together may have been one of life's accidents.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But it was a... precious one.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I ruined it... in a way I did not foresee.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I understand how deeply you treasure that time, Fiammetta. Your love burned so hot, it singed the hearts of those around you. I...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I always wanted to thank you for one thing. You were the one who taught me how to love Laterano.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But at the same time, I knew I would hurt you, and destroy what you so cherish.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I am a villain. It would be just for you to hate me.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Are you trying to piss me off, Andoain?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Whether or not I hate you is for me to decide, not you.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I understand that, and I am grateful for it. I am fortunate to have made a friend like you.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Go do what you need to do.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: But remember, I won't forgive you. I never will.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: These two are taking you to the Basilica, right, Andoain?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: It is I who is taking them, Lemuen.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Which means you're still determined to walk this path?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Of course I am.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Will it be dangerous?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Unknown might be the better word.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Have you ever thought of stopping?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Whether I am the captain who attacked you, or an arrogant, naive nurturer in a dream... My doubts, my fixations, my mistakes... They have all led me here.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I cannot stop.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Alright then.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: It's hard to call Laterano 'Paradise' the way it is now.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: That monster running rampant across the city, those strange things she reared wandering all over the place. Nobody really knows what's going on, or what will come next...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: The three of us need to work out a way to solve these issues and find El, who's gone missing. As for you, your wounds look rather serious...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You might die, Andoain. We might die.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: We've talked about Rocamarea, about its belltower and its rainy nights, about the mute child you buried in Sargon, about the miner's frozen legs you had to amputate in Ursus...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You told me about all sorts of places, and I remember them all.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I always pitied you. I understood many of your opinions, and I never disagreed with you, but I could never truly understand you. I was much the same for you.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: We are both clear on that matter, just as you know how grateful I am for your pity.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Well, I am a Lateran, aren't I?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: That is where you shine the brightest. I will always remember how you taught me to shoot a gun.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Speaking of, where is that gun now?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I left it in Laterano.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Ten years ago, it was your final mission with our team of commandos. Even if nothing had happened, you would still have left.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Which means these words came a little late, is all.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Right...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: It's been far too long since that day... And I'm glad of it. Gratitude and blame no longer hang so heavy.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Well then...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Farewell, Andoain.
Lemuen speaks no further. Mostima goes up to her wheelchair, looking Andoain square in the eyes.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: I know what you're about to say, no need to thank me. Farewell, 'Captain'.
Fiammetta looks at Andoain, then at her two friends. She stays silent.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Farewell.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Cardinal Lemuen, there are some tasks I must assign to the three of you.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: You doing alright, Fiammetta?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: ...I'm fine.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Fiammetta, I...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: This thing... might involve me, but I know it's not only my problem, or Andoain's. These past two years have taught me that.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Yeah, I should really learn that too.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Alright, enough about that. Right now... If what Federico says is true, the most important thing is to act quickly.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Good thing there's no arms control in real life. I can blast those monsters as soon as I see them.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I'll cover you, just like the old days.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Wait a sec, Lemuen.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Federico just said that Sanktas who attack them will Fall.

spans.text: said that Sanktas who attack them will Fall.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Falling's no walk in the park, trust me on that.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: About half of the people awake in the city are Sanktas. Without their numbers, we won't be able to stop such a large procession.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Unless...

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: We add in those fallen Angels and errari Federico mentioned.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Wait, he said they were pretty emotionally charged and didn't know what they were up to, not to mention that he's only got temporary command over them.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Not like they need steady nerves or pure intentions to help out. Relax, I'll handle them.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: I'm a Fallen Angel too, and I've spent lots of time outside of Laterano.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: We got any better choices for angel wrangler?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: It still won't be enough. The situation on the road from the Shrine of Nurtury to the Basilica is too complex. We need to get administrative permissions for the roadside facilities along the way ASAP.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I'll head back to the Seventh Tribunal for a bit.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: By yourself?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Don't trust my wheelchair skills?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You'll make me mad.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Quick, let her rub your ear tufts a bit.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Since the two of you have everything planned out, what else is there for me to add?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Let's split up... 'teammates'.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: We have to go now, children.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Hugo, help take care of our new Sankta friends, alright?

steps.name: Bolívarian Child
steps.text: Yes, Sister.

steps.name: Panicking Child
steps.text: Where did Senior Nurturer go?

steps.name: Fearful Child
steps.text: Did he stop caring about us?

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: He just has to go handle a few things for a little while.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Think about it. We don't know each other very well, so if he didn't promise me he'd come back, why would I agree to take care of you?

steps.name: Panicking Child
steps.text: Ohhh, you're right.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Right, would you like to hear the story of how the lost Zhayedan captured the Castle of Dreams?

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Or maybe how the Kheshig brought gold to marry the princess of Gaul, but the gold turned to sand storm, burying Lingones?

steps.name: Fearful Child
steps.text: Huh? That's not what we learned in history class...

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: They're not stories you'd hear in Laterano! I can tell them to you while we walk.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Here, some bread from Patia. You haven't eaten since we got into the city.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Making up tall tales for children again, Nueda?

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: I'm curious, do other K'uk'ulkan treasure the knowledge in your heads as much as you do?

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: I've never met another of my kind.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: If I can turn that knowledge into stories for children with a little tweaking, then it means there's still some use for it. Otherwise, it will just be a scattering of pale fragments in my mind.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Hmph. You have a surprisingly flexible mindset.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Oh, right, are you disappointed?

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: About what?

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: You traveled all this way to Laterano, to your holy land, but it wasn't apples and fireworks that welcomed you, or a loving God of universal salvation...

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Instead, you've got rampaging demons.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: I am disappointed... but not completely.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Have I ever told you how I became a nun, Aurela?

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Please do.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: As you know, I wandered all around Bolívar from a young age.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: It wasn't hard to survive, my knowledge proved useful on that front. As for my parents, even if I forgot what they looked like, they still managed to fill my head with lots of things.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: But I couldn't understand the more complicated parts. They pointed to the Black Flow, the far edge of the sea, the depths of the dunes of gold, even the space beyond the stars. They spoke of race after race, secret after secret...

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Not a good fit for a place like Bolívar.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Which is why I hate them, Aurela. Everywhere I look, I see soldiers fighting over men and money, artillery firing left and right, and Bolívarians caught in the crossfire...

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: And all I had were pale fragments.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Until I was thirteen, when I met a nun.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: A band of True Bolívarians guerrillas had robbed her. She was gravely injured, leaning against a rock and close to death.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: But when I got close, I could hear her singing.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Her bandages had fused with her festering wounds. She must have been in so much pain in the final moments of her life, yet she was still so serene...

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: It was a hymn, one that had always been in my mind, one that I had pored over in puzzlement countless times.

a.text: Abode of our Lord, font of parental love♪
He punishes evil and drives out injustice♪
All shall bask in His love♪
Whether they have scars or stones♪

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Until that very moment, when some of those pale fragments took on color and form, and came together into something called—

steps.name: Nueda & Aurela
steps.text: Laterano.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: So you took up her habit.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: I did.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Even if Paradise is pure and spotless white, to me, it cannot compare to the very first time I heard that hymn.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Good.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Nueda, forget everyone else, take the kids and follow that Patia girl. She looks like she knows her way around town.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Alright. Wait, you're staying at the Tower of Revelations?

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: But the executor said...

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: A long-since-Fallen Sankta doesn't need to listen to a saint.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: The night we fled Bolívar, I told you why I wanted to come back.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: R-Revenge.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: I saw that old bastard through my scope just now. He's at the head of the pack.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: I won't let him go.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: We all have our own obsessions when it comes to Laterano, Nueda.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It's strange, seeing the Basilica devoid of people.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Follow me, please, Arturia.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Here it is.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The pillars of scripture?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Between these two pillars is a slab engraved with The Saints' Travels. Press the halos of the saint statues in the same order as listed on the slab, then push this wall.

spans.text: Between these two pillars is a slab engraved with
. Press the halos of the saint statues in the same order as listed on the slab, then push this wall.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I have reported to His Holiness here many times before, but I never noticed this hidden mechanism.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Maybe because you've never doubted Laterano.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I hope what you are about to see will not sway your faith.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I'm looking forward to it already.
Andoain followed the Pope down here once.
They had passed the buried bones of saints, passed steles and statues showcasing their deeds, walked through thousands of years of Laterano before arriving at the end of history.
But...
Andoain suspects his memories are still in disarray.
The former white of the corridor is gone, entirely replaced with the dour, cold sheen of iron.
Statues of saints still line the path, but bizarrely-shaped lumps of machinery protrude from the walls, engulfing their arms, eyes and legs.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It seems like devils have had their way with our history.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I thank you for your warning, Andoain. I would have been much more surprised otherwise.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: No, this place has changed.
Andoain furrows his brow. Off in the distance, he sees a red light, blinking faintly. He knows what it is.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Do you see that red light?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: That's where we're going, but we should only be seeing it much further down this corridor...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Stay alert.
A cloaked guard suddenly appears. The moment he sees Federico, he starts firing. There is no room for negotiation.

steps.name: Shrine Patrol
steps.text: Alert.

steps.name: Shrine Patrol
steps.text: Repeat, alert. Intruders sighted, eliminating on site.
An ear-piercing siren begins to wail, as more and more guards file into the trio's field of view. Their blurry visages hide beneath their cloaks, like spirits in shadow...
While their halos shine all the more dazzling.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The guards protecting the Shrine of Nurtury in the dream are now here.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: This means... We're in the right place.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Stand behind me.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: This isn't the dream.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: It's obviously still reality, so why'd all the color...?

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: It's quiet here. We won't be disturbed by all the commotion over there.
She stands at the corner, looking out across the deathly silence, completely unguarded against you.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: But I don't like it, {@nickname}. It's perhaps too quiet.

spans.text: But I don't like it, {@nickname}. It's perhaps

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: But we have no other choice, do we?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (She's not limiting me, Doctor.)

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Amiya's not here. I can't guarantee I can hold her off... but I'll do my best—)

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Relax, you're safe.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: I won't allow you to be disturbed by the chaos these Sanktas caused.

options: I thought you were still locked up in Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: That doesn't matter, compared to what's currently on my mind.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Entering attack mode.)

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Sorry, Doctor, she might have shown up because of me...)

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (I never thought she'd catch onto me when I tried to access PCS—)

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Calamity? I see only the evolution of a species, the pointless struggle of life.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Everything happening in Laterano right now is a product of PCS's autonomous derivations.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: All I did was recalibrate it beforehand, returning it to its original purpose. Of course, it has adapted to the progress of the Originium project since.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Speaking of progress, ours has slowed far behind projections, {@nickname}.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Good to know you haven't lost your curiosity.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: PCS was an experiment developed using bionics, one that once offered many benefits to our soldiers and scientists.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: But it was left behind on Terra, and without long-term maintenance, its cognitive radiation amplifier entered partial standby mode, and its operational efficiency is now extremely reduced.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: But what's interesting is what happened after it came into contact with Terra's native species. It didn't have the effect I expected—

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Not only were its beneficiaries able to share their knowledge and emotion, but even their species-specific traits were assimilated. That never happened during our testing.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: A rather pleasant surprise, isn't it, {@nickname}?

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Good to know you haven't lost your curiosity.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: PCS was an experiment developed using bionics, though we were never able to understand its true nature. There was also the risk of it disrupting the subjects' cognitive functions when used—

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: But in the face of grim disaster, it was still brought into service ahead of schedule.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: It can reduce barriers to communication and strengthen the bonds between individuals, all while maintaining thinking abilities and personality...

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: This offered many benefits to our soldiers and scientists.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: It has been gathering dust since it was left behind on Terra, but as you know, {@nickname}, it is still far from operating to its full potential.

options: You mentioned it adapting to the Originium project's progress?
What connection does it have to the Originium project?

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Don't get excited, {@nickname}, I'll explain everything.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: However, your new companion seems like she has something to say to you.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Bad news, Doctor, I can't find a way out of here.)

options: If her goal is still Originium...
We might not be in Laterano anymore...
This might be the future of Laterano...

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: As keen an intuition as ever, but one that lacks basic knowledge.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: This is just a vision of a possible future I conjured up for you using the PCS system.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: No more time, no more color. A place locked in eternal stasis.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: It's rare for us to have a chance to walk together, {@nickname}. Come, leave behind these conflicts that have nothing to do with you.

options: No. You're afraid I'll access the PCS system.
You didn't expect me to show up here either.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: I sense... hate in your voice. I understand.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: It's because of AMa-10, your 'Kal'tsit'.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: You left in such a hurry last time. You still have many doubts you have not yet cleared, while I have many conjectures I must confirm with you.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Something's... strange about the way she's acting. Her expression's different from when she was back on the deck.)

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (I could try an attack—)

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Put away those talons.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: I respect that you've given yourself a name, 'Mon3tr', but I understand your fundamental underpinnings better than you do.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: If you want AMa-10 back, I can help you, {@nickname}. You know where to find me.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: I know that's what you want too, Mon3tr.

spans.text: I know that's what you want too,

options: Don't get taken in by her, Mon3tr!

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: You've always clung to the connection between matter and reality.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Originium is the language we created, so naturally, I can use it to make my words heard by whoever I want.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: It is so for you, and it is so for that machine—
'In response to me, it propagated, then created an even larger cache to perform a new round of calculations.'
'The machine operates on its installed logic, seeking the continuation of itself and its community that has achieved emotional resonance.'
'But in your haste, you decided this was an error to be stopped. Even those Sanktas regard it as rejection from the Law...'
'Follow me, {@nickname}.'
'Witness a true crisis with your own eyes.'

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Every department of the Curia has its own offices. The Basilica is merely ceremonial. There should not be such a complex space beneath it.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: We must perform one final round of testing.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You said you went down a one-way passage before, right, Andoain?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But we've changed direction six times, and now we're here again.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Seven, actually.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...We head back.
The three of them return to their former position. A platform, one where the white of a church blends with the black of machinery, wantonly streaked with red light emanating from an unknown source...

Disorder, chaos, imbalance, danger... No matter if from an architectural or religious point of view, shape and structure here has lost all meaning. They cannot stop themselves from wondering if they are still in Laterano.
Federico and Arturia stop walking at the same time. This is an exceedingly familiar experience. Before they met the Witch King, they wandered an infinite flight of stairs.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: There is no need to go any further.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: This is a derived structure that did not originally exist. While I do not know the principles or processes behind it, it has without a doubt warped space here.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: We are in an incomprehensible maze.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: He is preventing us from approaching.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Who?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: The God of the Sankta, the answer to everything.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Don't expose our position, Fede.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I don't sense any human emotions coming from them. Are they really Sanktas, or are they machines here to tidy up the maze?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: They are most likely the same as the organisms above ground. If ordinary Sanktas attack them, they will Fall.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The deeper we go, the more of them there are, and the stronger their... 'empathy' becomes.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: We beat back a wave of them, and that just draws in another... We'll end up completely overwhelmed.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The procession is moving at a fast pace, and will not need much time to arrive at the Basilica. It is highly unlikely Cardinal Lemuen's team will be able to stop their advance completely.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: We must learn the entire truth about this calamity. We have wasted too much time already.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Perhaps I may be of some use.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You are severely wounded.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I'll leave the patrols to the two of you.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But when it comes to pathfinding, I happen to be rather good at that.
Light gathers in Andoain's palm.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Arts?

steps.name: Injured Townsfolk
steps.text: *cough* Thank you, Andoain.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: You shouldn't go so far, Señor Jaime! I didn't see you all day! I only found out you came to the beach after asking around.

steps.name: Injured Townsfolk
steps.text: I just wanted to find something to eat... Didn't think the sea fog would be this thick.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Even if there wasn't any fog, pirates roam these parts!

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: You shouldn't leave Rocamarea just because you feel like it... At least... At least ask me to come with you next time.

steps.name: Injured Townsfolk
steps.text: Alright, alright... Speaking of, was that your Arts just now?

steps.name: Injured Townsfolk
steps.text: The fog was so dense, I couldn't even see my own shoes. I thought I'd be lost forever, but then a ray of light came by...

steps.name: Injured Townsfolk
steps.text: I-I thought someone managed to repair the local lighthouse or something!

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: No need to be so dramatic! I'm just glad I managed to help you.

steps.name: Injured Townsfolk
steps.text: But Andoain, I heard your people use guns, custom-made ones.

steps.name: Injured Townsfolk
steps.text: I also heard your homeland, that place called Laterano, is a universal Paradise...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: My home is Rocamarea. I was born here and raised here, Señor Jaime.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Let's go home. I'll carry the food.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: The light parts the dawn mist, and our quarry's line of sight is blocked. I will show the way. Now's your chance, Fiammetta.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Got them!

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Lemuen, Mostima, sweep the battlefield.

steps.name: Lemuen & Mostima
steps.text: Understood, Captain.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Not bad, Andoain, keeping a trick up your sleeve like that! There's way too many bandits in this gang. Without your Arts, we wouldn't have been able to resolve things this quickly.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: It's just an unconscious reaction. It got me and others out of trouble a few times, before I got my guardian gun.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Without it, I wouldn't have been able to find Laterano.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I nearly forgot you only got your gun the day before you joined the Pontifica Cohors... But you're pretty good with it! Can't tell you've never used it before!

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: It's a part of a Lateran's life, isn't it? I should be practiced with it.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Besides, as I've found out recently, guns and halos are what keep Laterano invincible. It doesn't need this glimmer of mine.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Talking about that stuff again, Andoain?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Haha, sorry.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: This operation's gone pretty off-the-rails compared to the original plan from the Pontifica Cohors. Should we write up the details as-is? Ah, whatever, I'm sure you'll polish up the final report.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But what about the places outside Laterano?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: How many Rocamareas, how many lonely islands are there beyond the reach of the faith?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I cannot forget. I can see...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Andoain?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Is it Laterano, or...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: No, no, there is no difference.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: If, through the spiritual light, even the darkest stain can be cleansed; if, with a pious heart, even a savage monster can wade out of the mud...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Does that not mean there are no lonely islands beyond the reach of the faith?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Then why is it that all I've seen, everyone I've known, couldn't be saved? There must be something missing, something I overlooked...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: A path.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Not a power, nor a place, but simply... a path, a path that leads from present torments to future salvation.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I-If you can show me the future, then you must know the path that leads to it. Tell me, show it to me...
The colossus of nothingness swims through gaps in space-time. It does not respond to Andoain.
The details of that strange yet oh-so-real sight begin to warp and flow with Its silence, and everything is smeared with a thick layer of clouds.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: No, no...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I need to know more!

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Can you hear what I'm saying, Andoain?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Put that thing down...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: No, Lemuen. You don't know what I saw. I can't stop here!
Light bursts forth from Andoain's hand, like a plant rushing headlong into season, blooming as if about to wither.
He wants to part the clouds. He wants to see the revelation in all clarity. He wants to grasp onto the possibility.
From then on, once more did he set foot on a journey, bearing sin and evil upon his back. He guided foreign believers to Laterano, searching for an answer.
But he had no time to share what he saw, the truth that nearly shook him to his core.
He had walked so many paths, yet what was the one thing that remained constant?
He will always remember that year, the year the salt wind buried his home, and the emotions he bore in his heart as he left Rocamarea—
That was the starting point of his journey.

The sounds of the executor fighting the patrols do not stop. Andoain does not hold back as he casts his Arts, an endless font of light flowing from his body, winding its way into the depths of the maze.
Rather than a harsh light, it is gentle, perhaps even dim, like sunlight caressing a patch of autumn leaves, tracing the paths through which they fall.
He asks himself: 'Pathfinder, where does this path end?'
Until finally...
A glaring red light cuts off his Arts.
Once, he saw this alongside Yvangelista XI. Once, he found himself shaken...
The light is more icy, more piercing, more dangerous than before.
But Andoain does not close his eyes.
He knows that cold machine is his Lord, his god, the foundation of his faith.
Andoain faces God. He does not turn away.
He has sought and he has lost. He has pondered and he has doubted.
A sharp pain runs through him. It only takes a moment for his vision to go dark, but at the same time...
He hears God's answer.
